`interface IAssetLocator`<br/>
**Known subtypes:** [`FileAssetLocator`](/reference/resources/fileassetlocator/), [`StreamAssetLocator`](/reference/resources/streamassetlocator/), [`StringAssetLocator`](/reference/resources/stringassetlocator/), [`SnapshotUrlAssetLocator`](/reference/testing/snapshoturlassetlocator/)<br/>
**Package:** `dev.joid.lib.asset.locator` · **Module:** `core` · **Source:** [IAssetLocator.java](https://github.com/Zeldown/JOID/blob/main/core/src/main/java/dev/joid/lib/asset/locator/IAssetLocator.java)

Turns one kind of input into an `Asset`, so that every loader of JOID accepts it.

## Description

Register it with [`AssetLocator.register`](/reference/resources/assetlocator/#AssetLocator-method-register).
Return an asset with a stable id, such as a [`ClasspathAsset`](/reference/resources/classpathasset/), so that the caches and a reload find the same content.

## Method details

<a id="IAssetLocator-method-supports"></a>

### supports

`boolean supports(Object handle)` <span class="joid-qualifier">abstract</span>

If `true`, this locator turns `handle` into an asset.

<a id="IAssetLocator-method-locate"></a>

### locate

`Asset locate(Object handle)` <span class="joid-qualifier">abstract</span>

Returns the asset of `handle`; JOID calls it only when `supports` returned `true`.
Throw `IllegalArgumentException` when the input names nothing: the resource then fails instead of loading.
